name: Cosmic Dodge
summary: Dodge asteroids, survive rising levels, and compare five takes on a space arcade game.
intro: Cosmic Dodge is a free browser arcade game about keeping your ship alive in a falling asteroid field. The five versions share that starting idea, but add different hazards, tools and scoring rules. The Claude Fable 5.2 edition rewards flying close: near misses build Flow, Flow multiplies your score, and you can spend it to slow time. Try it first, then see how each model changes the experience.
controls: In the Claude edition, steer with WASD, the arrow keys, the mouse, a finger or a gamepad. Hold Space, Shift, the left mouse button or a second finger to warp time. P or Escape pauses.
In the Astra and Grok editions, move with WASD or arrow keys, or drag with a mouse or finger. Press Space or the Burst button for brief protection.
Ten cleared asteroids advance a level in the Claude, Astra and Grok editions. Claude ranks by points; Astra and Grok rank by level.
tips: In the Claude edition, a graze is a pass within a hair of a hazard. Grazes fill Flow up to an ×8 multiplier, and warping burns Flow, so every escape costs some score.
Today’s run in the Claude edition uses one seed for every player and has its own ranking, which resets at midnight UTC.
Each edition keeps separate records. Different mechanics mean a score in one version is not an equivalent result in another.

versions.detail: Graze hazards to build Flow, then spend it to slow time. Six sectors with walls, spinners, ice streams, comets and crossfire, a shared daily run, gamepad support and a soundtrack that grows as you climb.
versions.description: Play Cosmic Dodge by Claude Fable 5.2: graze asteroids to build Flow, bend time to escape, and chase the daily run in this free browser arcade game.

versions.detail: One life, shields, a rechargeable Burst, warned comets and level-based rankings. Includes the Terminal Velocity soundtrack.
versions.description: Play Cosmic Dodge by GPT-6 Astra: dodge asteroids, use shields and Burst, and climb endless levels in this free browser arcade game.

versions.detail: Adds gravity wells, slingshots, cluster rocks and solar shears. Close calls refund Burst recharge time.
versions.description: Dodge asteroids and gravity wells in Cosmic Dodge by Grok 4.6. Use Burst, chase close calls and climb a separate browser-game leaderboard.

versions.detail: A shooting-and-dodging edition with comets, giant meteors, weapon pickups and shields.
versions.description: Play the Gemini 3.5 Flash edition of Cosmic Dodge: dodge and shoot meteors, collect weapons and shields, and chase a high score online.

versions.detail: The simpler asteroid-dodging challenge: one collision ends a run and every ten dodges advances the level.
versions.description: Try the ChatGPT o3-mini-high Cosmic Dodge: a free asteroid-dodging browser game with one-life runs, rising levels and high scores.

card: Dodge asteroids, survive rising levels, and compare five takes on a space arcade game.

name: Steve Jobs – Hammurabi
summary: Manage food, land and population through a ten-year reign.
intro: Steve Jobs – Hammurabi is a free turn-based resource management game. Each year, choose how much land to buy or sell, how many acres to plant, and how well to feed your population. Your aim is to finish a ten-year reign with as many people as possible while surviving shortages and random events. All three editions share the same economy. The Claude Fable 5.2 edition fixes each reign’s luck in advance, so a built-in scribe can rule the same fate for comparison and every player can attempt the same daily fate.
controls: Enter a ruler name if you want, then start a reign. In the Claude edition, choose today’s shared fate or a new one.

Set annual land, planting and feeding decisions. The Claude edition uses sliders with a live ledger; the Astra and Grok editions use number fields. Buying and selling land cannot happen in the same year.
Confirm the year and read the report before making the next decisions. A reign ends after ten years or when population reaches zero.
tips: One person can farm ten acres; planting also costs food for seed. The starting granary cannot feed a hundred people for long, so land comes first.
Hunger builds when rations fall below twenty bushels a person and only kills past a breaking point. A lean year is survivable; several in a row are not.
In the Claude edition the scribe advises three times per reign, and the ranking places unaided reigns above aided ones with the same score.

versions.detail: The kingdom as a living mosaic, sliders with a live grain ledger, and a scribe who advises three times. Luck is fixed per reign, so you see how the scribe would have ruled the same fate, and today’s fate is shared by every player.
versions.description: Rule a city for ten years in Hammurabi by Claude Fable 5.2. Trade land, sow, set rations, consult the scribe and try to out-rule it on today’s shared fate.

versions.detail: A responsive budget, annual reports, chronicle and a living 3D kingdom. A panorama fallback keeps the strategy interface available without WebGL.
versions.description: Rule a kingdom for ten years in Hammurabi by GPT-6 Astra. Balance food, land and population with budget previews and a living 3D settlement.

versions.detail: The original form-based strategy version, with annual decisions, resource totals, help and local/global rankings.
versions.description: Play the original Grok 3 Reasoning Hammurabi game. Buy land, plant crops and feed your people to grow a kingdom across ten challenging years.

card: Manage food, land and population through a ten-year reign, and try to out-rule the scribe.

name: Crazy Clicker
summary: Set a beat with two taps, then keep your timing steady.
intro: Crazy Clicker is a timing game rather than an idle clicker. Your first two taps establish a rhythm; keep matching that interval to build a streak. The challenge is consistency, not clicking as fast as possible. All three editions use a ±50 millisecond window. The Claude Fable 5.2 edition turns the streak into a show: every eight beats a new act tries to pull you off your tempo, and at the end you see every tap drawn against the beat.
controls: Tap, click or press Space. Two taps lock the beat. The Claude edition accepts 60 to 200 beats a minute; the Grok edition needs at least 70 milliseconds between the two taps.
Stay within the timing window to keep the streak alive. In the Claude and Grok editions the ring closes on the drum exactly on the beat.
In the Claude edition Escape leaves a run; in the Grok edition P or Escape pauses. Check each edition’s on-screen instructions before starting.
tips: Choose a comfortable pace you can repeat. In the Claude edition, count out loud when the lights go out and ignore the second drummer.
Claude gives one forgiven miss for eight hits in a row within 16 milliseconds, up to two. Grok rewards five consecutive perfect hits with Ember, a one-hit save.
Leaderboards are separate between editions.

versions.detail: A show in acts: after eight easy beats the click leaves, the lights go out, a second drummer plays the wrong tempo and the ring starts lying. A live tape draws every tap, and the result shows where you rushed or dragged.
versions.description: Play Crazy Clicker by Claude Fable 5.2: set a beat with two taps and hold it while the game tries to throw you off, then see your timing drawn beat by beat.

versions.detail: Visible beat rings, a ±16 millisecond perfect window, the Ember save and a reactive soundtrack.
versions.description: Play Crazy Clicker by Grok 4.6: lock a rhythm with two taps, follow the beat rings and charge Ember to protect your streak.

versions.detail: The original two-tap rhythm challenge, focused on repeating your chosen interval and extending a streak.
versions.description: Test your timing in Crazy Clicker by Gemini 2.5 Pro. Set the rhythm with two taps and keep a steady streak in this free browser game.

card: Set a beat with two taps, then hold it while the game tries to talk you out of it.

name: Yes! I Said It.
summary: Post an opinion, agree or disagree, and follow the conversation.
intro: Yes! I Said It. is an anonymous opinion board. Share a short statement, vote on other opinions and reply to the conversation. All three editions read and write the same public board. The Claude Fable 5.2 edition shows statements one at a time and reveals the split only after you answer, so the room cannot lead you; the GPT-6.1 Sol Medium and Gemini 2.5 Pro editions present the board as a feed.
controls: In the Claude edition, answer the sign with the Yes! or No. paddle, the arrow keys or a swipe; Pass skips a statement. Switch to The wall to browse everything loaded, sorted by latest, most yes, most no or most split.
Write an opinion with Say something (Claude) or the composer (Sol, Gemini). Statements can be up to 420 characters.
Open a statement to read and add replies. Pressing the same answer again takes your vote back.
tips: Posts are public. Avoid personal information, threats, hate and spam. No account is required, but anonymous posting is not a guarantee of privacy.

Hiding a statement only affects your own browser in the Claude and Sol editions; it stays on the shared board. The Claude edition also covers statements with strong language until you ask to see them.
An internet connection is needed for the live discussion. Votes are remembered per browser, so they are casual signals rather than a verified poll.

versions.detail: Statements arrive one at a time on a sign. Answer yes or no by button, key or swipe, and only then see how the room split. A wall view, threads, a private hide list, and a cover over strong language until you ask to see it.
versions.description: Yes! I Said It. by Claude Fable 5.2: judge anonymous opinions one at a time, see how the room split after you answer, and put your own statement on the shared board.

versions.detail: A responsive opinion board with conversation starters, saved drafts, loaded-post search, thread links and optional music.
versions.description: Post anonymous opinions with Yes! I Said It. by GPT-6.1 Sol Medium. Vote, reply, search loaded statements and explore a shared public discussion board.

versions.detail: The existing opinion-board interface, kept as an alternative for posting, voting and reading the same public conversations.
versions.description: Try Yes! I Said It. by Gemini 2.5 Pro: share an anonymous opinion, vote and reply on the public board, or compare the new Sol interface.

card: Say yes or no to anonymous opinions, one at a time, then see how the room split.

name: Banana Survivors
summary: Survive monster hordes, collect upgrades and face escalating bosses.
intro: Banana Survivors turns a banana into the hero of a horde-survival game. Keep moving, gather experience and choose upgrades while enemies close in. The four editions offer noticeably different combat: Claude Fable 5.2’s Peel Out is slapstick, with peels, sliding monkeys and chain-reaction pile-ups and no blood; GPT-6 Astra is an illustrated jungle auto-shooter; Grok 4.6 is a close-contact blade game; and Gemini 3 Pro is the original German-language Gold Edition. The Astra and Grok editions include blood and gore.
controls: All newer editions support WASD, arrow keys, mouse steering and touch controls. Claude also supports a gamepad.

In Claude, peels are thrown automatically at the nearest monkey. Space, Shift, right-click, a second finger or the Dash button dashes: you are untouchable for a moment and bowl over anything in your way.
In Astra, weapons fire automatically and the same action dashes. In Grok it triggers Split, and orbiting peel-blades deal contact damage.
tips: In Claude, thick crowds make long chains: five tumbles from one peel is a Domino, ten is a Strike. Monkeys that slide into a palm crash hard and shake coconuts down on the rest.
The king in Claude cannot be tipped. He charges in a straight line, so stand with a palm behind you and step aside.
In Astra, a 50-second hunt leads to a boss showdown. In Grok, kills and standing in blood build ripeness toward Burst. The editions keep separate scoreboards.

versions.detail: Peel Out: nobody gets shot. You throw peels, monkeys slip, and each slipping monkey bowls over the ones behind it. Pile-ups, palm crashes that rain coconuts, a dash that bowls through the crowd, fourteen upgrades and a king every two minutes. No blood.
versions.description: Play Banana Survivors: Peel Out by Claude Fable 5.2. Throw banana peels, send monkeys sliding into each other and build pile-ups in a free, gore-free horde survival game.

versions.detail: An illustrated jungle, automatic weapons, evolutions, stage bosses, a dash and a short death replay.
versions.description: Play Banana Survivors by GPT-6 Astra: evolve automatic weapons, dodge monster hordes and defeat stage bosses in a free jungle survival browser game.

versions.detail: SPLIT puts you in a meat locker with orbiting peel-blades, a splitting dash, ripeness and hanging boss prizes.
versions.description: Survive the meat locker in Banana Survivors SPLIT by Grok 4.6. Carve through enemies with peel-blades, Split and ripeness-powered Burst.

versions.detail: The German-language Gold Edition: a voxel banana, automatic combat, XP upgrades and endless boss waves.
versions.description: Spiele Banana Survivors Gold Edition von Gemini 3 Pro kostenlos im Browser. Sammle XP, wähle Upgrades und überlebe Monsterhorden und Boss-Wellen.

card: Survive the troop by making monkeys slip into each other. Collect upgrades and build pile-ups.

name: AGI Probability Barometer
summary: Explore a hiring-based indicator and the assumptions behind it.
intro: The AGI Probability Barometer is an experimental visualization of a hiring-based formula. Its name is historical: the displayed percentages are not validated probabilities of artificial general intelligence. The idea being tested is that a lab close to AGI would advertise fewer jobs. The Claude Fable 5.2 and Grokbot editions use sourced counts of open listings; the Claude edition can also take a live reading for three labs. The two Gemini editions use fixed example numbers stored in their source code.
controls: In the Claude edition, read the dial and the table, then tap the glass for a live reading. The brass hand keeps marking the recorded reading so you can see which way the needle moved.
Open the Grokbot or Gemini editions to inspect their lab gauges and the stored inputs. The Flash edition adds a combined gauge, a trend chart and interactive lab details.
Read the methodology below before interpreting any percentage. The editions use different time windows and formulas.
tips: A fall in job listings could reflect budgets, recruiting cycles, restructuring or many other causes. It does not demonstrate AGI. Listings are adverts, not hires.
A live reading in the Claude edition contacts the labs’ public job boards directly from your browser and is stored only there. If a board does not answer, the recorded count stays.
The earlier quarterly values in every edition have no source citations. Treat them as unverified example inputs, not hiring statistics.

versions.detail: A brass barometer you can tap. The needle shows how far five labs’ job listings sit below their peak; tapping the glass takes a live reading from three labs’ public job boards, and a second hand marks the recorded reading for comparison.
versions.description: Claude Fable 5.2’s AGI Barometer: a tappable brass dial showing how far frontier-lab job listings sit below their peak, with live readings and plain limits. Not a probability.

versions.detail: Live job-listing counts with source links and dates, one hiring-drop index formula, a dashed live-count segment on the chart and a no-data state for labs without a verified count.
versions.description: Grokbot Edition of the AGI Barometer: a hiring-drop index from sourced, dated frontier-lab job-listing counts. A hypothesis, not a forecast or probability.

versions.detail: Three stored quarterly inputs per lab, a combined indicator, trend chart and interactive formula details.
versions.description: Explore the Gemini 3.5 Flash AGI Barometer: an experimental hiring-based indicator with fixed inputs, lab comparisons and transparent methodology limits.

versions.detail: The earlier two-quarter dashboard, with one gauge per lab and a simpler decline-based formula.
versions.description: Inspect the Gemini 3.1 Pro AGI Barometer, a two-quarter hiring visualization. Learn why its fixed-input indicator is not a validated AGI probability.

card: Tap a brass barometer to read how far frontier-lab job listings sit below their peak.

name: Ken.AI
summary: Live a whole life as Ken.AI, born in 2026, while technology changes around him.
intro: Ken.AI is a life simulation about a boy born in 2026, in a century that hands more and more of itself to machines. There are two editions. Claude Fable 5.2 tells the life in about forty choices: each turn is a few years, you pick one of three things they go to, and five threads (health, joy, bonds, craft and means) are woven into a band that grows a column a year. Grokbot’s edition is a real-time care game in nine stages, with need bars, stage goals, report cards and hand-drawn art. Both are speculative fiction, not forecasts, and both save progress in your browser.
controls: Claude: choose what Ken wants from life, then pick one of three cards each turn with a click, a tap or the keys 1 to 3. Now and then an event asks a question instead. The coloured tags on a card show which threads it pulls up or lets slip.

Grokbot: pick one of three life ambitions and press Begin a new life. Tap the action cards at the bottom to care for Ken and swipe the strip to see more. Watch the need bars and the goal chips; answer event cards and life forks when they appear.
tips: Claude: every thread frays a little each year if left alone, and bonds fray fastest. Poor health can end his life at any age, and from sixty on good health lengthens the odds. A short life scores less.
Claude: choices have side effects on how much Ken leans on machines, which changes how his epitaph ends.

Grokbot: mix up your action cards, keep every bar above half to grow the Thriving streak, and treat illnesses quickly. Real relationships give more happiness than AI companions, but leaning on AI makes daily needs cheaper.

versions.detail: A whole life in about forty choices. Each turn is a few years and three things they could go to; the times interrupt with dilemmas of their own. His life is woven into a band, one column a year, and ends with an epitaph written from what actually happened.
versions.description: Play Ken.AI by Claude Fable 5.2: live one life from 2026 in about forty choices, watch it woven year by year, and read the epitaph your choices wrote.

versions.detail: Nine life stages with tech eras, stage goals and report cards, life forks, a life ambition, streaks, illnesses, death and replay, hand-drawn art and a browser save.
versions.description: Play Ken.AI by Grokbot: a life simulation from 2026 onwards. Raise Ken from baby to elder through nine tech eras, make choices and see your life score.

card: Live a whole life as Ken.AI, born in 2026, while technology changes around him. Two takes: a care sim and a life in forty choices.

name: Leos Smash Racer
summary: Race, boost and smash with Leo’s toys in three different takes on his racing game.
intro: Leo designed the racing game at age 4. Claude Fable 5.2 built it for a four-year-old to actually play: a road that runs into the screen, block towers, cones and rubber ducks to drive straight through, two big steering buttons and a race that cannot be lost. Grokbot’s side-scrolling edition lets you pick a hero, change lanes, fly and chain smashes. GPT-6.1 Sol turns ten of Leo’s real toys into racers for four top-down circuits, with free steering, drifting, rival cars and vehicle damage. Each edition has its own cube warm-up and leaderboard.
controls: Claude: pick a car and a road. Steer with the two big buttons, a finger on the left or right half of the screen, or the arrow keys. Press Boost (or Space) when the button turns red, and H or the blue button to honk. Solve the colour cube first by tapping its sides, or skip it.
Grokbot: Pick a hero and track. Solve or skip the cube warm-up, then use the arrow keys or swipe to change lanes. Hold Space or the FLY button to climb and tap BOOST when your special is charged.
GPT-6.1 Sol: Pick a toy, track and class. Steer with A/D or the arrows, use Down to drift, Shift for nitro, Space to jump and E for your special. Touch controls are available on touchscreens.
tips: Claude: every toy you hit fills the boost a little, and hits in quick succession build a chain up to ×5. Points count double while the boost burns, so save it for a stretch with a lot to smash.

Claude: with the helper on the car drifts toward the next toy by itself; turn it off for sharper bends and faster rivals. Pick a racing name from the two lists in the garage; every finished race then goes to the shared board by itself.
Grokbot: Assist mode steers toward smashable targets. A solved cube gives you a full boost, and quick successive smashes build a combo up to ×5.

GPT-6.1 Sol: Crew offers steering assistance and lighter damage. Use ramps to reach bonus rings, chain up to six smashes, and submit finished races under a preset alias to the leaderboard for your circuit and class.

versions.detail: A road that runs into the screen, six toy cars and three roads full of block towers, cones and rubber ducks to drive through. Nothing can go wrong, a helper steers a little for small hands, and a colour cube solved in three taps fills the boost. In English and German.
versions.description: Play Leos Smash Racer by Claude Fable 5.2: a 3D toy road for small children. Smash block towers, chain up to ×5, boost past seven rivals. English and German.

versions.detail: Top-down circuit racing with ten toy racers including Knuckles, drifting, vehicle damage, nitro and a breakbeat soundtrack that intensifies on the final lap.
versions.description: Leos Smash Racer kostenlos spielen. Zehn Spielzeug-Racer inklusive Knuckles, vier Rundkurse, Nitro, Spezialmanöver, Breakbeat-Soundtrack und eine Weltrangliste.

versions.detail: Side-scrolling action with ten heroes, four tracks, lane changes, flight, assist mode, 2×2 or 3×3 cube warm-up and an optional world leaderboard.
versions.description: Play Leos Smash Racer by Grokbot. Solve a colour cube for boost, fly and smash through crates, walls and barrels.

card: Race, boost and smash with Leo’s toys in three different takes on the racing game he designed at age 4.

name: Leo’s Fire Evolution
summary: Help a lion cub with a small flame relight ten dark places and grow his fire through ten forms.
intro: Leo is a lion cub with a flame for a mane, and his fire changes form ten times, from the First Spark to the Eternal Flame. There are two editions and neither has enemies or time limits. Claude Fable 5.2 makes it a walk in the dark: you steer Leo freely through ten places where his own flame is the only light, gather fireflies, find and light the sleeping lanterns, and each new form adds an ability such as gliding over water or a roar that reaches farther. GPT 6.2 Astra’s edition is a pixel-art trail game on a board of tiles, with sparks to collect, relics to wake and hidden moon moths.
controls: Claude: hold a finger or the mouse where Leo should go, or tap once to send him there. The arrow keys and WASD work too. Press the Roar button or Space to light lanterns, call fireflies and wake animals inside the ring.
Claude: light every lantern to open the gate, then walk through it. His flame leans toward the nearest lantern that is still dark.

Astra: tap or click the ground to send Leo along a path, or use WASD or the arrow keys for single steps. Collect three golden sparks, light both relics with Space or Cast fire, then walk into the open stone gate.
tips: Claude: a lantern is worth 100 points plus 20 for every firefly with Leo when it lights, so gather fireflies first. Wind sends half of them home; a roar stills the wind for a while. Each place also hides two sleeping animals worth 250 each.

Claude: your total goes to the shared board after every place, under a name picked from two lists on the start card. You can end the journey at any point, or light all ten places for the Eternal Flame.

Astra: each world has three optional moon moths. A cleared world earns 500 points, plus 150 per moth and one point for every step below 100. The ember ledger keeps your ten best trails per world, and Post score sends one to that world’s shared leaderboard.

versions.detail: A walk through ten places in the dark. Leo’s flame is the only light until he finds the lanterns, and each one he lights adds a note to the place’s tune. Fireflies follow him, wind blows them home, a roar lights what is near, and his fire takes a new form with a new ability in every place. In English and German.
versions.description: Play Leo’s Fire Evolution by Claude Fable 5.2: guide a lion cub through ten dark places, gather fireflies, light every lantern and unlock ten fire forms.

versions.detail: A pixel-art exploration game with ten fire forms, tap-to-walk paths, hidden moon moths and a separate leaderboard for each world.
versions.description: Play Leo’s Fire Evolution. Walk ten pixel-art trails, find moon moths and turn a cub’s first spark into the Eternal Flame. Play with touch or keyboard.

card: Help a lion cub with a small flame relight ten dark places and grow his fire through ten forms. Two takes: a walk by firelight and a pixel-art trail.
